newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses slip from peaks, dollar steadies.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses slip from peaks, dollar steadies.

text.p: Leading European bourses slipped back from record or near-record levels by midsession on Wednesday, with Paris suffering a reversal of more than three percent, largely on bad news on corporate taxes.

On the currency market, the dollar regained some strength after being hit by a rush into the yen after news of the flotation of the Thai baht. It also advanced to its highest for more than three years against the mark.
But the bullion market was under pressure, with gold hitting its lowest level since March 1993 amid speculative selling.

New records scored earlier in the day on the Frankfurt, Paris and Milan bourses, adding to a strong advance the previous day, were prompted by progress on Wall Street on Tuesday and strength in the dollar -- good news for exporters.

But the Paris bourse, having gained 1.4 percent to a new record level, took a big hit after government spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann confirmed that the new Socialist-led coalition was studying new company taxes.

"The prime minister recalled that if efforts are needed to promote solidarity and to contribute to economic recovery, then they should be shared by the different players in the economy -- public ones but also companies," she said after a weekly cabinet meeting.
"Sure it is negative for the market but it is not a big surprise. I see our options people shouting down the phone but I do not understand this fall," one Paris stockbroker said.

Shares in Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel were briefly suspended limit-up after jumping more than 20 percent on news that France and Britain could extend its licence to 99 years. Eurotunnel was later up 7.25 percent at 7.40 francs after an early high of 8.40.

The London stock market, Europe's biggest, had followed a 2.7 percent leap on Tuesday to rise within five points of its record level on the FTSE 100 index on Wednesday on the belief that it would get its wish for a tough government budget to cap inflation.
But it soon slid back ahead of a tough first budget expected from the new British Labour government in mid-afternoon.
"The budget will be much more threatening than people expect," said Charterhouse chief economist, Richard Jeffrey.
"There is enough bid speculation around to get market-makers going but the closer the budget gets, the fewer bets people will take and it tends to get very quiet on budget days," he said.
The Frankfurt bourse was up around 0.80 percent but much of the gains had been seen in after-hours computerised trade on Tuesday and shares were below their morning highs.
Milan was around one percent higher after advancing 1.8 percent to record levels earlier.
The British pound tested 2.90 marks ahead of the budget, up from 2.8880 at the previous close.
The yen became a safe haven after the Bank of Thailand said it was dropping its pegged rates system against a basket of currencies and allowing the market to set rates.

"Whenever a developing currency is allowed to float, there is always some fear in the market and that causes a capital outflow, and in the Asian region the safe haven is obviously the yen," said Alessandra Stagliano, economist at Daiwa Europe.

"The fact Thailand has floated its currency could be the prelude to more countries moving, which would provide support for the yen, although that will take time to feed through," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International.
In reaction the dollar sank to a session low of 114.15 yen, although it later recovered somewhat as the surprise wore off, while staying below its previous European closing level.

"There seems to have been a lot of profit-taking in dollar/yen (overnight) and right now people are reluctant to push it to 115 yen...because of perceptions that authorities are happy with dollar/yen where it is," said Deborah Read, economic advisor at Bank of America in London.
Elsewhere, currency traders did not anticipate any change in interest rates from a meeting of the U.S. central bank's Federal Open Market Committee which ends on Wednesday.

"We don't see anything happening that might jolt the dollar out of its current range. There's no major influence coming from the FOMC and everybody seems comfortable with the dollar's recent range," Stagliano said.
Lyons said U.S. non-farm payrolls data, due on Thursday, could be of more interest to the market.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was at 114.52 yen and 1.7500 marks, compared with 114.90 and 1.7421 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0945 GMT

LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 2.4 points at 4,730.7, having earlier hit 4,791.1, just below its all-time high of 4,796.0 reached in mid-June, but also shown a loss on the day of more than 12 points at one stage.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 39.61 points at 2,904.43 after an earlier record 2,986.09.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 30.59 points at 3,850.44 after a record 3,871.13 earlier.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed at a 4-1/4 year low of $331.45 an ounce and later traded around $331.75 against $333.65 at Tuesday's close after Australian producer selling and amid market concern about possible central bank selling. Silver was down two cents at $4.65.
